title: Measure before changing code
summary: A performance measurement is a clue about a real task.
introduction: A performance measurement is a clue about a real task. Your task: Choose one page action you want to measure.
learningObjectives: Choose one page action you want to measure.
Explain the example for measure before changing code

blocks.text: A performance measurement is a clue about a real task. A slow phone and a fast laptop may get different results from the same page.

Use a local test page and browser developer tools. Code samples show a page choice or a measurement. Compare before and after under the same conditions; exact timings depend on the device and network.

blocks.code:
Choose one page and one task.
Record the device and network setting.
Load it several times.
Write down what feels slow.
Change one cause and repeat the same test.
blocks.title: Measure before changing code

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: Recording the device and network makes the measurement repeatable.
Changing one suspected cause at a time helps connect an improvement to that change.

blocks.text: A fair comparison can show whether a change helped that task instead of only changing a number by chance.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not compare one fast cached visit with one slow first visit and call it a fair test.
